missing_readings: A point whose value is null, absent or unreadable is left out of the chart and counted in `spec.dropped`, which the renderer shows under the plot; a series with no readings left is left out; a spec with nothing left to draw is refused (no_points). A gap is never drawn as zero and a broken number is never read approximately.
not_repaired: single quotes and unquoted keys: guessing what they meant could change a value
a number with a unit in it ("6.2 h")
a body cut short inside a string, because finishing a label would invent one
notes: The ayuvo-chart fenced block Coach may emit, and the exact system-prompt section that teaches it. Both platforms embed a verbatim copy and a parity test byte-compares it with this file. scripts/coach_reference.py parse_chart_spec is the executable grammar; where this file and the reference disagree, the reference wins. A spec is read after repair_chart_json, and the keys and type spellings below are accepted alongside the ones the prompt teaches: strictness is about parity between the two phones, not about punishing a model for punctuation.
point_forms: a bare number, whose label becomes its 1-based position

prompt.charts_section:
## Charts
When a number is easier to see than to read, draw it. Emit a fenced block tagged `ayuvo-chart` holding one JSON object; the app renders it as a native chart.

```ayuvo-chart
{"type":"bar","title":"Sleep last 7 nights","unit":"h","labels":["Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat","Sun"],"series":[{"label":"Asleep","values":[6.2,7.1,5.4,7.8,6.6,8.1,7.3]}]}
```

- `type` is one of bar, grouped_bar, stacked_bar, line, area, pie, scatter, range, progress.
- Optional: `title`, `unit`, `x_label`, `y_label`, `note`, and `max` for progress.
- At most 4 series and 60 points per series. Every value must be a plain finite number.
- Write each value as JSON writes numbers: one decimal point at most, no units and no quotes (6.6, never 6.6.6 or "6.6 h"), and close every bracket you open. A value the app cannot read is left out of the chart and the chart says so.
- Put the x labels in `labels` and each series' numbers in `values`, in the same order and the same length. (A `points` list of `[label, value]` pairs is also accepted.)
- Put one chart in its own block and keep explaining in normal text around it.

Every value in a chart must come from a tool result, the user's own message or a file they attached. Never estimate, extrapolate or fill a gap to make a chart look complete: leave the day out instead, and say in the text that it is missing. If you do not have real numbers, do not draw a chart.
prompt.guardrails:
Chart guardrails:
- A chart repeats data you already have; it never introduces a number you did not read from a tool, the user's message or an attachment.
- Days, weeks or readings with no data are omitted from the chart, never drawn as zero.
- Keep labels short (a weekday, a date, a test name); the chart is read on a phone.

repairs: a comma directly before } or ] is dropped
NaN, Infinity, -Infinity and undefined become null, which means 'no reading'
a quote glued to the end of a number (5.38") is dropped, since it can never start a string
a number token that is not a number (7.1.0, 01) becomes null for the same reason
prose after the root value is dropped, and a body that was cut short has its open containers closed

types.area: One series filled under the line. Same point shape as line.
types.bar: One series of labelled bars. points: [[label, value], ...].
types.grouped_bar: Two to four series sharing the same labels, drawn side by side.
types.line: One to four series over shared labels.
types.pie: Exactly one series; every point is a slice.
types.progress: Exactly one series; each point is a value against `max`.
types.range: One series where every point carries y and y2 (low and high).
types.scatter: One to four series of independent points.
types.stacked_bar: Two to four series stacked on the same labels.
